note:
Meals whose protein was PUBLISHED, not estimated — a canteen board or a package panel. This is the only ground truth the protein table can honestly be graded against. The golden set's `protein_g` was an annotator's rough figure written per serving under the retired count x size x portion ladder; when the set was re-annotated in absolute grams those figures stopped corresponding to their own weights, and 14 of 36 came to imply impossible densities (chicken schnitzel at 3.4 g per 100 g). A table graded against a guess measures agreement with the guess.

Items are annotated the same way the golden set is: edible weight on the plate, read off the photograph. So a gap here is the table AND the weight together, which is the number a person actually sees. Where a meal's published figure excludes part of the tray, `excludes` says so and those items are left out.

Two meals is not a calibration set. It is the start of one, and the honest thing to do with a table tuned on two points is not much. Add a row every time a meal arrives with a printed number.
